'''Orly Alter''' ([[Hebrew language|Hebrew]]: אורלי אלטר) is an Israeli-American physicist, geneticist, and mathematician, and a [[USTAR]] associate professor of [[bioengineering]] and [[human genetics]] at the [[Scientific Computing and Imaging Institute]] and the Huntsman Cancer Institute at the [[University of Utah]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=ORLY ALTER – Home – Faculty Profile – The University of Utah |url=https://profiles.faculty.utah.edu/u0729867#bio |access-date=2023-03-13 |website=faculty.utah.edu}}</ref> She has published on quantum measurement, genomic signal processing, and tensor decompositions.

== Education and career ==
Alter began attending school at [[Tel Aviv University]] in Israel and graduated in October 1989 ''magna cum laude'' with her bachelors of science in physics.<ref name=":0" /> After receiving her undergraduate degree, she began pursuing her Ph.D. in applied physics at the [[Stanford University]] in California, USA. She completed her Ph.D. with a thesis on "Impossibility of Determining the Quantum Wavefunction of a Single System and a Fundamental Limit to External Force Detection," under the mentorship of [[Yoshihisa Yamamoto (scientist)|Yoshihisa Yamamoto]] in January 1999<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=Impossibility of determining the quantum wavefunction of a single system and a fundamental limit to external force detection |url=https://searchworks.stanford.edu/view/4028357 |date=1999 |first=Orly |last=Alter}}</ref> and then moved onto a postdoctoral fellowship in genetics, remaining at Stanford.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation 1999 Annual Report |url=https://sloan.org/storage/app/media/files/annual_reports/1999_annual_report.pdf |access-date=2025-02-05 |website=sloan.org}}</ref> Alter moved to the [[University of Utah]] in 2010, where she joined the Scientific Computing and Imaging Institute as a USTAR Associate Professor of Bioengineering.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Orly Alter Joins the Scientific Computing and Imaging Institute as a USTAR Associate Professor of Bioengineering |url=https://www.sci.utah.edu/the-institute/news/329-orly-ustar.html |access-date=2024-05-24 |website=www.sci.utah.edu |date=13 August 2010 }}</ref>

Following this, she became a member of Cancer Control and Population Sciences Program, and was co-founder and [[Chief Scientific Officer]] of Prism AI Therapeutics in 2024.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Alter |first1=Orly |title=Orly Alter – Curriculum Vitae |url=https://alterlab.org/orly/CV.html |website=alterlab.org}}</ref>

== Research ==
Alter has one published book named ''Quantum Measurement of a Single System,''<ref>{{Cite book |last=Alter |first=Orly |title=Quantum Measurement of a Single System |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-3527617128}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Donald |first1=Matthew J. |title=Book Review – Quantum Measurement of a Single System by Orly Alter and Yoshihisa Yamamoto |url=https://people.bss.phy.cam.ac.uk/~mjd1014/qmss.pdf |website=people.bss.phy.cam.ac.uk |access-date=8 March 2025 |date=February 2002}}</ref> co-authored with Yamamoto, and another book in preparation, ''Genomic Signal Processing: Discovery of Principles of Nature from Matrix and Tensor Modeling of Large-Scale Molecular Biological Data.''<ref>{{Cite book |last=Alter |first=Orly |title=Genomic Signal Processing: Discovery of Principles of Nature from Matrix and Tensor Modeling |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-1119078371}}</ref> Alter's work on finding patterns in DNA finds predictors indicative of a woman's risk for ovarian cancer,<ref>{{Cite news |date=February 2016 |title=Increasing Accuracy of Diagnosis, Prognosis |work=USA Today; Farmingdale |pages=8 |id={{ProQuest|<!-- Add ProQuest data here -->}} |volume=144 |issue=2849}}</ref> and she uses mathematical models to improve the outcomes for women with ovarian cancer.<ref>{{Cite news |date=15 Apr 2015 |title=U. researchers' mathematical models could provide better ovarian cancer treatment, outcomes |work=The Salt Lake Tribune; Salt Lake City, Utah |id={{ProQuest|<!-- Add ProQuest data here -->}} }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Big Data, Hidden Knowledge |url=https://thepathologist.com/issues/2015/articles/jun/big-data-hidden-knowledge/ |website=The Pathologist |publisher=Texere Publishing |access-date=12 March 2025 |language=en |date=15 June 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Calculating Cancer Cures |url=https://nae.edu/File.aspx?id=134900&amp;File.mp3 |website=National Academy of Engineering (NAE) Innovation Podcast and Radio Series |publisher=NAE in Collaboration with [[WTOP-FM|WTOP Radio]] |access-date=12 March 2025 |language=en |date=19 April 2019}}</ref>

Alter's team identified a DNA pattern as a predictor of survival in [[glioblastoma]] patients using new mathematical methods, which was reported in 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=Genome-wide pattern found in tumors from brain cancer patients predicts life expectancy |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/477030 |website=EurekAlert! |publisher=University of Utah Health |access-date=8 March 2025 |language=en |date=15 May 2020}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
In 2005 Alter was selected by the [[International Linear Algebra Society]] to give the Linear Algebra and its Applications Lecture.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LAA-lecturers |url=https://ilasic.org/laa-lecturers/ |access-date=2024-05-24 |website=International Linear Algebra Society |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Alter |first1=Orly |title=Genomic Signal Processing: From Matrix Algebra to Genetic Networks |editor1-last=Shader |editor1-first=Bryan L. |journal=The Bulletin of the International Linear Algebra Society |date=Fall 2005 |issue=35 |pages=2–14 |url=https://ilasic.org/wp-content/uploads/IMAGE/image35.pdf}}</ref> Alter was an [[American Association of Physicists in Medicine]] Science Council Session Winner in 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=AAPM Science Council Session Winner (SCSW) Recipients |url=https://aapm.org/org/history/SCSessionWinners.asp |website=aapm.org |access-date=8 March 2025}}</ref>
